question.problem:
Given the function $y=2{x}^{3}+x-3{log}_{6}⁡x,$ find the instantaneous rate of change at $x=3.$ Do not round the answer.

The instantaneous rate of change at $x=3$ is
{{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
To differentiate a logarithm with base $a,$ we use the formula

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({log}_{a}⁡x)=\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡a}.
$$

To find the instantaneous rate of change at a given point, we have to find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ at that point.

Taking the derivative we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2{x}^{3}+x-3{log}_{6}⁡x) \\  & =2\cdot 3{x}^{2}+1-3\cdot \frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡6} \\  & =6{x}^{2}+1-\frac{3}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡6}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the instantaneous rate of change at $x=3$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=3} & ={(6{x}^{2}+1-\frac{3}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡6})|}_{x=3} \\  & =6(3)^{2}+1-\frac{3}{3\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡6} \\  & =55-\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡6}\,.\end{aligned}
$$
